sentences.text: Ms Saritha Achary - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Mukesh Shukla - Government Advocate for the respo
Heard on I.A. No.15958/2024 an application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
The appeal is time barred by 11 days.
For the reasons stated in I.A. No.15958/2024, the same is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
Heard on the question of admission The appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A. No.15957/2024 which is first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 26.08.2023 passed by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Dindori (M.P.) in S.T. No.32/2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.1000/-
with default stipulation.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant that the present appellant is in continuous custody since 06.05.2020 which has been stated in para 25 of the impugned judgment and from the date of judgment he is also in custody.

It is also submitted that the prosecutrix though stated in chief examination that the 2 CRA-14216-2023 present appellant has forcibly committed rape with her but in cross-examination she categorically admitted that her father had taken Rs.10,000/- as advance from the present appellant and present appellant demanded the money but her father could not repay the same.
It is also submitted that due to such demand, a dispute arose between the present appellant and father of the prosecutrix one week prior to the incident.
In para 5, she categorically admitted that on the date of offence, the present appellant - Sultan was not in the village.
In para 6 she categorically admitted that Sultan has not committed any wrong with her.

Though the DNA report is positive and Dr.Mini Morvi (PW-6) has also stated that there was forceful rape with the prosecutrix but keeping in view the aforesaid facts and also the period of custody, he has good case on merits.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
It is also submitted that the present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal.

It is prayed Sultan Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187058907/
1 that the benefit of suspension of sentence be granted and the appellant be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A.
No.15957/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail.
The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 11.05.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard.
List this case for final disposal in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
